results.summary: This is a factory test module hardened with LibreLane 3.0.0.dev38. It provides three modes: mirroring input pins to outputs, mirroring bidirectional pins to outputs, and outputting an 8-bit counter on both output and bidirectional pins. The mode is selected by rst_n and sel signals. It is used to verify the connectivity and functionality of all I/O pins on the ASIC.

This design measures human reaction time with microsecond precision using a VGA monitor and a single button. It displays a green screen after a random delay, and the user must press the button as quickly as possible; pressing too early results in a red screen. The design requires a Tiny VGA PMOD and a pulled-up button connected to ui[0]. It is an ASIC adaptation of the r0 project, optimized for area, and includes an LFSR debug block that appears as noise when idle.

This project implements a Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) unit using a Dadda multiplier and a Kogge-Stone adder for high-performance digital signal processing. It performs multiplication and accumulation operations, essential for filtering and convolution. The design is verified through a provided testbench that simulates various input scenarios. No external hardware is required beyond standard clock and reset signals.

This design is an 8-bit Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) unit with a specialized SPST adder for efficient addition. It multiplies two 8-bit inputs to produce a 16-bit product, which is accumulated in an internal register. The lower 8 bits are continuously output, while the upper 8 bits are available on a bidirectional bus that can be externally overridden. It is optimized for Tiny Tapeout's limited IO and minimal area, and can be tested with simulation testbenches or Cocotb.

This is a bit-serial implementation of a subset of the PDP-8 computer, adapted from a textbook example and using one-hot state encoding generated by VITO. It emulates instructions such as AND, TAD, ISZ, DCA, JMP, and microinstructions, with a reduced memory of 128 words accessed serially. The design requires an external serial memory emulation, typically via a Python testbench, and includes wait states to accommodate cocotb testing. It is an educational project demonstrating computer architecture and hardware design.

This project implements a JTAG TAP controller compliant with IEEE 1149.1, supporting bypass, IDCODE, and boundary scan register instructions. It manages shifting, capturing, and updating of instruction and data registers via TDI, TMS, and TCLK. The TDO output reflects the serial data shifted out of the selected register. It is intended for testing and debugging of digital circuits.

This design accepts a byte from a UART input and produces a chirp waveform as an 8-bit parallel output, using LoRa-style modulation with a bandwidth of 125 kHz and spreading factor 8. It requires a UART transmitter, a 10 MHz clock source, and a digital signal analyzer for testing. The chirp is output on uo[7:0], and a done signal is available on uio[0]. The design is intended for generating chirp signals for communication or testing purposes.

This is an SPI test design based on the tt07_alu_74181 project, featuring two read/write 8-bit registers and two read-only status registers. The first read/write register drives a 7-segment display. It is tested using an RP2040's SPI master, with example code provided to write and read registers. No external hardware is required beyond the RP2040 and the demoboard.

This design plays raw unsigned 8-bit PCM audio samples from an attached SPI flash chip through DACs connected to analog pins ua[0] and ua[1]. It requires an SPI flash configured for 24-bit addressing and audio amplifiers connected to the analog outputs. The design supports play/pause control and mode selection via input pins. It is notable for integrating analog output with digital SPI flash reading.

This project implements a Built-In Self-Test (BIST) mechanism for an 8-bit by 16-word internal SRAM. It uses a finite state machine to write a test pattern to all addresses and then read back and compare the values, setting a fail flag on mismatch and a done flag upon completion. The test pattern is provided on ui_in[3:0], and the start signal initiates the process. It is intended for memory integrity verification and can be tested with a Cocotb testbench.
